safi-cedvel:55-59.t:
* I'rab:
(هذا) a demonstrative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "للمؤمنين" [Note: Some allowed the demonstrative to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "الأمر هذا".], (للطاغين) attached to the khabar of (إنّ). (اللام) is for emphasis. (شرّ) is the noun of (إنّ), accusative (manṣūb).
Clause: «هذا (للمؤمنين) ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
Clause: «إنّ للطاغين لشرّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(56) (جهنّم) is a badal (substitute) for شرّ - or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it - accusative. (الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition; the maxṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm (the one specified for condemnation) is omitted, its implied form being "هي", that is, جهنّم.
Clause: «يصلونها ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial) from جهنّم.
Clause: «بئس المهاد ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the implied condition, that is: "if this is its state, then how evil a resting place it is" [Note: It is possible that the clause is resumptive.].
(57) (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is حميم [Note: Or it is a direct object of an omitted verb which يذوقوه explains; and it is possible that the khabar of (هذا) is implied, i.e. "this is a punishment", with (حميم) being the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ.]. (الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida), for alerting; (اللام) is the lām of command.
Clause: «هذا ... حميم» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
Clause: «يذوقوه» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
(58) (الواو) is a conjunction. (آخر) is a mubtadaʾ, nominative. (من شكله) is attached to an adjective of آخر. (أزواج) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ آخر.
Clause: «آخر من شكله أزواج» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هذا ... حميم.
(59) (معكم) is an adverbial, accusative, attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in مقتحم [Note: Or a ḥāl from فوج, which is then qualified.]. (لا) is negative. (مرحبا) is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أتيتم" [Note: Or an absolute object of an omitted verb.]. (بهم) is attached to an adjective of (مرحبا) [Note: Or attached to the miming verbal noun (مرحبا).].
Clause: «هذا فوج ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of a saying, of an implied "saying".
Clause: «لا مرحبا بهم» has no grammatical position; parenthetical [Note: Or it is the content of an implied saying, namely the saying of the chiefs whom the Qur'an referred to with the address pronoun in the word (معكم); and the clause of saying is a ḥāl.].
Clause: «إنّهم صالو ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory of cause.

* Morphology:
(57) غسّاق: a noun for what flows from a wound as pus or matter; its verb is غسق, of the class ضرب; its pattern is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(شكله): a noun for the form in which a thing is; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(59) مقتحم: an active participle from the quinquiliteral verb اقتحم; its pattern is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(مرحبا): a noun of place from the triliteral رحب; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the ʿayn because its imperfect has ḍamma on the ʿayn ... or it is a miming verbal noun from the sound triliteral.
(صالو): plural of صال ... see verse (163) of Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt. It has undergone ʿilāl by deletion: its lām was deleted because it met the wāw of the nominative marker as a quiescent letter; its origin is صاليو, after making it quiescent and moving its vowel to the preceding letter; its pattern is فاعو.

* Benefits:
- The redundant fāʾ:
This is the one whose presence in speech is like its absence. Sībawayh does not accept this, while al-Akhfash allowed its redundancy in the khabar without restriction, and reported: «أخوك فوجد». Al-Farrāʾ, al-Aʿlam and a group restricted the permissibility to the khabar being a command or a prohibition. The command is as in the verse:
وقائلة: خولان فانكح بناتهم ... وأكرومة الحيين خلو كما هي
(Said by one: "Khawlān - so marry their daughters; and the noble pride of the two tribes is vacant as it was.")
Al-Zajjāj interpreted on this basis the words of Allah the Exalted in the verse before us: هذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ. The prohibition is like «زيد فلا تضربه». Ibn Burhān said: The fāʾ is made redundant according to all our colleagues, as in the verse of al-Namir ibn Tawlab:
لا تجزعي إن منفس أهلكته ... فإذا هلكت فعند ذلك فاجزعي
(Do not grieve if I have destroyed a precious possession; but when I perish, then grieve at that time.)
And among its redundant uses is the poet's verse:
لما اتقى بيد عظيم جرمها ... فتركت ضاحي جلدها يتذبذب
(When he guarded himself with a hand whose offence was great, I left the exposed part of its skin quivering.)
because the fāʾ does not enter the apodosis of لما, contrary to Ibn Mālik.

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) is for turning away from what precedes (iḍrāb). (لا مرحبا بكم) is like لا مرحبا بهم [Note: in the preceding verse (59).]; the wāw in (قدّمتموه) is redundant, being the lengthening of the vowel of the mīm. (لنا) is attached to (قدّمتموه). (فبئس القرار) is like فبئس المهاد [Note: in verse (56) of this sūra.] in its words and clauses.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive. The content of the saying is omitted, i.e. "do not revile us, but you ..."
Clause: «أنتم لا مرحبا بكم» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
Clause: «لا مرحبا بكم» is in the position of accusative, the content of a saying, of an implied "saying", i.e. "you are more deserving of the saying: no welcome to you", so the khabar of (أنتم) is implied.
Clause: «أنتم قدّمتموه ... » has no grammatical position; explanatory of cause.
Clause: «قدّمتموه لنا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(لنا) is attached to (قدّم). (الفاء) links the apodosis of the condition. (عذابا) is a second direct object, accusative. (ضعفا) is an adjective of (عذابا). (في النار) is attached to (زده) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (زده), or from (عذابا).].
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
Clause of the vocative and its response ... is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
Clause: «من قدّم ... » has no grammatical position; the response to a vocative.
Clause: «قدّم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
Clause: «زده ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of the condition, accompanied by the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:62-63.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive - or a conjunction. (ما) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ. (لنا) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (لا) is negative. (من الأشرار) is attached to (نعدّهم) [Note: Or attached to an omitted second direct object.].
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: Or conjoined to the clause قالوا in the preceding verse (61).].
Clause: «ما لنا ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
Clause: «لا نرى ... » is in the position of accusative, ḥāl from the pronoun in (لنا).
Clause: «كنّا نعدّهم ... » is in the position of accusative, an adjective of (رجالا).
Clause: «نعدّهم ... » is in the position of accusative, the khabar of كنّا.
(63) (الهمزة) is for interrogation. (سخريّا) is a second direct object, accusative. (أم) is a conjunction, the connected (muttaṣila) one. (عنهم) is attached to (زاغت).
Clause: «اتّخذناهم سخريّا» has no grammatical position; a resumptive within the sphere of the saying.
Clause: «زاغت عنهم الأبصار» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause اتّخذناهم.

* Morphology:
(الأشرار): plural of شرير, pattern فعيل with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a lightened kasra on the ʿayn; an assimilated adjective from the triliteral (شرّ), of the classes نصر, ضرب and فتح. It is pluralised on أفعال; since its ʿayn and lām are the same letter, the kasra was moved to the fāʾ, so the shīn was given kasra. As for شرّير with kasra on the shīn and a doubled rāʾ, it is an intensive of the active participle, and its plural is شرّيرون.

safi-cedvel:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
The demonstrative in (ذلك) points to what was related of the states of the disbelievers. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (تخاصم) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو".
Clause: «إنّ ذلك لحق ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
Clause: «تخاصم ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(تخاصم): the regular maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quinquiliteral تخاصم; it is on the pattern of its past verb with ḍamma on the letter before the last.

* Rhetoric:
Simile: in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ ذلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ».
He likened their exchange of words and the questions and answers passing between them to what passes between disputants in the like.

safi-cedvel:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) is "restraining and restrained" (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (إله) is genitive in form, nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ. (إلّا) is for restriction. (الله) is the khabar, nominative. (الواحد، القهّار، ربّ، العزيز، الغفار) are adjectives of the name of Majesty, nominative. (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of genitive, conjoined to السموات.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
Clause: «أنا منذر ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
Clause: «ما من إله إلّا الله ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of the saying.

* Morphology:
(الغفّار): an intensive of the active participle from the verb غفر, of the class ضرب; its pattern is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a doubled, vowelled (fatḥa) ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:67-70.t:
* I'rab:
(عنه) is attached to (معرضون). (ما) is negative. (لي) is attached to the khabar of كان. (علم) is genitive in form, nominative in position, the noun of كان. (بالملإ) is attached to علم. (إذ) is an adverb of past time, attached to an implied word that is the muḍāf of الملأ, i.e. "knowledge of the speech of the Highest Assembly" ... (إن) is negative. (إليّ) is attached to (يوحى). (إلّا) is for restriction. (أنّما) is "restraining and restrained" (kāffa wa-makfūfa) ..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّما أنا نذير ... ) is in the position of nominative, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يوحى.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
Clause: «هو نبأ ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
Clause: «أنتم عنه معرضون» is in the position of nominative, a second adjective of نبأ.
Clause: «ما كان لي من علم ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
Clause: «يختصمون» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «يوحى إليّ ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Benefits:
- The dispute of the Highest Assembly:
The angels disputed over the matter of Ādam, peace be upon him, when Allah the Exalted said إِنِّي جاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً, and they said أَتَجْعَلُ فِيها مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيها وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّماءَ. If you ask: how can it be said that the angels disputed because of their saying: أَتَجْعَلُ فِيها مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيها وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّماءَ, when disputing with Allah the Exalted is neither fitting nor possible? I say: There is no doubt that a question and an answer took place there, and that resembles disputation and debate, and this is the ground for the permissibility of figurative usage; for this reason the use of the word "dispute" is good.
On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "My Lord came to me in the best form" - he said: I think he said, in a dream - "and said: O Muḥammad, do you know about what the Highest Assembly disputes? I said: No. He said: Then He placed His hand between my shoulders until I felt its coolness between my breasts" - or he said: "in my chest - and I came to know what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. He said: O Muḥammad, do you know about what the Highest Assembly disputes? I said: Yes, about the expiations (that is, the good deeds that expiate sins). And the expiations are: staying in the mosques after the prayers, walking on foot to the congregations, and performing the ablution completely despite disagreeable conditions. Whoever does that lives in goodness and dies in goodness, and comes out of his sin as on the day his mother bore him. And He said: O Muḥammad, when you pray, say: O Allah, I ask You to do good deeds, to abandon evil deeds, and for love of the poor; and when You intend a trial for Your servants, take me to You without being tried. He said: And the degrees: spreading the greeting of peace, feeding food, and praying at night while people sleep." In one narration: "I said: At Your service, at Your service, twice," and in it: "and I came to know what is between the east and the west." Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: A good, gharīb ḥadīth. The scholars have two positions on this ḥadīth and on others like it among the ḥadīths of the attributes:
(a) The position of the Salaf: It requires believing in it as it came, without asking how (takyīf), without likening (tashbīh) and without divesting (taʿṭīl), and believing in it without interpretation (taʾwīl), and remaining silent about it and its like, while believing that Allah the Exalted لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ.
(b) The second position: It is to interpret the ḥadīth in a way befitting the majesty of Allah, negating from Him every deficiency, and that there is nothing like Him. They interpreted the ḥadīth to mean that "hand" stands for favour, benefaction and mercy, and that is common in the language of the Arabs. Its meaning on this basis is a report of Allah the Exalted's honouring him and favouring him by expanding his breast, illuminating his heart, and making him know what no one else knows, until he found the coolness of the favour and the knowledge in his heart; that is, when He illuminated his heart and expanded his breast, he came to know what is in the heavens and what is on the earth through Allah the Exalted informing him. His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it: Be, and it is. For it is not permissible for Allah the Exalted, nor for the attributes of His essence, to have contact, touch or deficiency; and this is more fitting for His transcendence, and the ḥadīth is to be understood accordingly. And if we take the ḥadīth to refer to a dream, the difficulty disappears and the purpose is achieved, and we have no need of interpretation; and seeing the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, in a dream with fine attributes is evidence of glad tidings, goodness and mercy for the one who sees it.

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(كتاب) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هذا" (this); (إليك) is attached to (أنزلناه); (مبارك) is a second khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كتاب, because it is an adjective and the operator in it is the demonstrative.]; (اللام) is the lām of cause; (يدّبروا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the sign of the accusative is the omission of the nūn..
And the (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يدّبّروا) is in the position of genitive after the (اللام), attached to (أنزلناه).
The (الواو) is a conjunction; (ليتذكّر) is like (ليدّبّروا); (أولو) is the fāʿil, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw, since it is attached to the sound masculine plural.
Clause: «(هذا) كتاب ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أنزلناه..» is in the position of nominative as an adjective of كتاب.
And the clause «يدّبّروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle (أن).
And the clause «يتذكّر أولو ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second implied particle (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يتذكّر..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أنزلناه), because it is conjoined to the first maṣdar.

safi-cedvel:30-34.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (لداود) is attached to (وهبنا); and the subject of praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, its implied form being سليمان (Solomon) - or داود (David) - Clause: «وهبنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «نعم العبد ...» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause «إنّه أوّاب ...» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
(31) (إذ) is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) in the position of accusative, a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember) [Note: it is permissible for it to be an adverbial attached to أوّاب.]; (عليه) is attached to (عرض); (بالعشيّ) is attached to (عرض); (الصافنات) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (الجياد) is a badal (substitute) for الصافنات - or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it - nominative.
And the clause «عرض عليه ... الصافنات» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
(32) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (حبّ) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is an ism maṣdar (noun of the verbal noun) [Note: or it is a direct object whose operator is أحببت, by implying in it the meaning of "I preferred" or "I wanted", with (عن) meaning على.. There are other, remote interpretations.]; (عن ذكر) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of أحببت, i.e. "distracted"; (حتّى) is a particle of limit and of genitive; (بالحجاب) is attached to (توارت), by implying in it the meaning of "it concealed itself".
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن توارت) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (أحببت).
And the clause «قال ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause «عرض ...»
And the clause «إنّي أحببت ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause «أحببت ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «توارت ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied literal particle (أن).
(33) (عليّ) is attached to (ردّوها); (طفق) is a defective past verb, and its ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to Solomon; (مسحا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. "he wiped them (wiping)" [Note: or it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, and this is the choice of al-ʿUkbarī.]; (بالسوق) is attached to the implied (يمسح) [Note: or it is attached to the maṣdar (مسحا), the object of the wiping being omitted, i.e. his hand.. There is another interpretation of the verse: striking the necks of the horses and their legs with the sword; then the (الباء) in his words (بالسوق) is redundant (zāʾida), and السوق is accusative in position as the direct object of the wiping.]
And the clause «ردّوها ...» has no grammatical position; it is a resumptive clause within the scope of the preceding saying.
And the clause «طفق مسحا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "so they brought them back, and he began wiping ..."
And the clause «(يمسحها) مسحا» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of طفق.
(34) (الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) is a particle of confirmation; (على كرسيّه) is attached to (ألقينا); (جسدا) is a direct object, accusative [Note: or a ḥāl from the implied object, i.e. "we cast him as a body", the pronoun referring to Solomon or to his son.]; and the agent of (أناب) refers to Solomon.
And the clause «فتنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to a resumptive clause at the beginning of the story [Note: or the clause is resumptive in the course of the narrative.] And the clause «ألقينا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis of the oath.
And the clause «أناب ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.:
"So Solomon went out and his people did not recognise him.. then he turned in repentance."

* Morphology:
(31) الصافنات: plural of الصافنة or الصافن, an active participle from the triliteral صفن (al-faras, "the horse stood") of the bāb ضرب, when it stands on three legs and rests the fourth on the edge of the hoof; its wazn is فاعل.
(الجياد): plural of جواد, a name for the horse, male or female; the wazn of جواد is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and the wazn of الجياد is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ, and it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change): its origin is جواد; the wāw was vowelled and what precedes it had kasra, so it was turned into yāʾ and became (جياد) ... And it is said that الجياد is the plural of جيّد, or the plural of جيد, which is the neck.
(32) حبّ: either a maṣdar of the triliteral حبّ or an ism maṣdar from the quadriliteral أحبّ; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn, and its ʿayn and lām are from one letter.
(الخير): a noun meaning wealth, and what is meant by it is horses; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. Al-Farrāʾ said: الخير and الخيل are the same in the speech of the Arabs.
(33) مسحا: a samāʿī (heard, not rule-based) maṣdar of the verb مسح of the bāb فتح; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, and it also means cutting.
(السوق): plural of ساق.. (see verse 44 of Sūrat al-Naml).

* Benefits:
- The trial of Solomon, peace be upon him:
The narrators have reported about Solomon, peace be upon him, things that do not befit the rank of prophethood and that no sound mind would believe, and these reports appear to be the weaving of the Jews, who persistently blackened the reputation of the prophets and attacked their dignity. Among these reports is what they mentioned: that Solomon, peace be upon him, raided a king at sea and married his daughter; she began weeping for her father, so the devils made for him a statue in the likeness of her father and dressed the statue in clothes resembling her father's clothes; then she, with her maidservants, kept prostrating to it for forty days without Solomon knowing. Then he entered upon his wife - Amīna - and forgot his ring; so the devil Ṣakhr came, took on the form of Solomon, peace be upon him, took the ring, and sat on the throne of his kingdom for forty days; and after his affair was uncovered he fled and threw the ring into the sea, a fish swallowed it, Solomon took the fish, slit open its belly, took the ring and returned to his kingdom; he ordered that the devil Ṣakhr be brought, put him inside a rock and sealed it over him with another, then bound them with iron and lead, and then ordered that they throw him into the sea. And so on to the end of the legend, which appears - leaving no room for doubt - to be a product of imagination and of the slanders of the Jews, who have not ceased to attack the prophets and the pure. Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and other verifying scholars said: What the narrators transmitted is not sound: that the devil took the likeness of Solomon ﷺ, was given power over his kingdom, and acted unjustly in his judgment over his community; the devils are not given power over the like of this, and Allah the Exalted has protected the prophets from such a thing. And what the verifying scholars held is that the cause of his trial was what
the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim) relate in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Solomon said: "Tonight I shall go round to ninety women, each of whom will bring a horseman who fights in the way of Allah the Exalted." His companion said to him: "Say: if Allah wills." But he did not say "if Allah wills," so he went round to all of them, and none of them conceived except one woman, who brought forth half a man. And by Allah, in Whose hand is my soul, had he said "if Allah wills," they would all have fought in the way of Allah as horsemen. In another narration: "I shall go round to a hundred women," and the angel said to him: "Say: if Allah wills," but he did not say it and forgot. The scholars said: The "half" (shiqq) is the body that was cast upon his throne, and this was his punishment and his trial, because he did not make the exception, being absorbed by eagerness and overcome by wishful longing,
and it was said: he forgot to make the exception, as is established in the ḥadīth, so that the command of Allah and His purpose regarding him might be carried out. And Allah knows best. The meaning of "he did not make the exception" (lam yastathni) is: he did not say "if Allah wills."

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) is a vocative muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ that is omitted for lightness ... and the (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (لي) is attached to (اغفر); the second (لي) is attached to (هب); (لا) is negative; (لأحد) is attached to (ينبغي); (من بعدي) is attached to an adjective of أحد; (أنت) is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ [Note: or an emphatic pronoun for the attached pronoun, the ism of إنّ, borrowed for the position of accusative.], its khabar being (الوهّاب).
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the vocative clause and its response.. is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «اغفر ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause «هب ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اغفر.
And the clause «لا ينبغي ...» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of (ملكا).
And the clause «إنّك أنت الوهّاب» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
And the clause «أنت الوّهاب ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:36-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (له) is attached to (سخّرنا); (بأمره) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تجري; (رخاء) is a ḥāl, accusative, from الريح; (حيث) is an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of accusative, attached to (تجري).
Clause: «سخّرنا..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال [Note: in the preceding verse (35).].
And the clause «تجري ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from الريح.
And the clause «أصاب..» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
(37-39) (الواو) is a conjunction; (الشياطين) is conjoined to الريح, accusative; (كلّ) is a badal (part-of-whole) from الشياطين.. (الواو) is a conjunction; (آخرين) is conjoined to كلّ, hence accusative; (في الأصفاد) is attached to مقرّنين; (الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis; (أو) is a conjunction of option; (بغير) is attached to a ḥāl from (عطاؤنا) [Note: or a ḥāl from the agent of امنن, or from the agent of أمسك.].
And the clause «هذا عطاؤنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, confirming the content of what preceded [Note: or it is the content of an implied saying, i.e. "We said to him: this is our gift.." and the implied saying is resumptive.].
And the clause «امنن ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you wish to bestow, then bestow".
And the clause «أمسك ...» is conjoined to the clause امنن.
(40) (الواو) is a ḥāl wāw; (إنّ له ... مآب): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (25) of this sūra.].
And the clause «إنّ له ... لزلفى..» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of سخّرنا.

* Morphology:
(36) رخاء: a sifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral رخا of the bāb نصر, the bāb فرح and the bāb كرم; its wazn is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and it contains the substitution of the weak letter - the lām of the word - by a hamza because it occurs word-finally after a quiescent alif; its origin is رخاو or رخاي.
(37) بنّاء: an intensive form of the active participle from the verb بنى of the bāb ضرب; its wazn is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and it contains the substitution of the weak letter by a hamza after the quiescent alif.
(غوّاص): an intensive form of the active participle from the triliteral غاص of the bāb نصر; its wazn is فعّال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (أيوب) is an ʿaṭf bayān on عبدنا, accusative; (إذ) is an adverb in the position of accusative, a badal from عبدنا; (بنصب) is attached to (مسّني)..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّي مسّني الشيطان..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted (باء), attached to (نادى).
Clause: «اذكر ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the implied clause اذكر إذ عرض عليه ... in verse (34):].
And the clause «نادى ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «مسّني الشيطان ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.

* Morphology:
(نصب): it is said to be the plural of نصب (with two fatḥas), and it is said to be a dialectal variant of النصب, like الحزن and الحزن (with ḍamma then sukūn in the first and two fatḥas in the second); a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb نصب ينصب of the bāb فرح, meaning "to be weary".

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(برجلك) is attached to (اركض), by implying in it the meaning of "strike"; (شراب) is conjoined to مغتسل, nominative like it.
Clause: «اركض برجلك ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying of an implied saying, i.e.: "We said: stamp ..."
And the clause «هذا مغتسل ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying of another implied saying, i.e. "so We said: this is a place of washing.." and between the two sayings there is implied speech, i.e.: "so he struck the earth, and a spring of water gushed forth, so We said ..."

* Morphology:
(مغتسل): a passive participle meaning "water", from the five-letter verb اغتسل; its wazn is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.. It may also be a noun of place.
(بارد): an active participle from the triliteral (برد) of the bāb نصر; its wazn is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:43-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction in the three places; (له) is attached to (وهبنا); (مثلهم) is conjoined to أهله, accusative; (معهم) is an accusative adverb attached to a ḥāl from مثلهم; (رحمة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative; (منّا) is attached to an adjective of رحمة; (لأولي) is attached to ذكرى.
Clause: «وهبنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.:
"We removed what afflicted him and gave him ..."
(44) (الواو) is a conjunction in both places; (بيدك) is attached to a ḥāl from (ضغثا) [Note: or attached to (خذ).]; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (به) is attached to (اضرب); (لا) is a negative jussive particle; (إنّا) is a particle resembling the verb, and its ism; (صابرا) is a second direct object, accusative; (نعم العبد إنّه أوّاب): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (30) of this sūra.].
And the clause «خذ ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying of an implied saying, i.e.:
"We said: take.." and the implied saying clause has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause وهبنا.
And the clause «اضرب ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause خذ.
And the clause «لا تحنث ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause اضرب.
And the clause «إنّا وجدناه....» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive - or giving a reason - and the clause «وجدناه ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «نعم العبد ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّه أوّاب ...» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.

* Morphology:
(ضغثا): a noun for a small bundle of grass or twigs; its wazn is فعل with kasra then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- Fulfilling an oath:
It is related that Job's wife - peace be upon him - was slow in returning to him one day over a need of his, so he swore that he would strike his wife a hundred lashes if he recovered. Allah then released him from his oath by the lightest thing for him and for her, because of her good service, and commanded him to take a bundle (ḍighth, a bunch of grass) containing a hundred small stalks and strike her with it a single blow; he did so and did not break his oath. Is this juristic ruling for Job in particular or for us in general? There are two opinions: one is that this ruling is general, and Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said this; the other is that it is specific to Job, as Mujāhid said. The jurists differed regarding one who swears to strike his slave a hundred lashes, then gathers them and strikes him with them in a single blow.
Mālik, al-Layth ibn Saʿd and Aḥmad said: he does not fulfil his oath; and Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī said: if he strikes him a single blow and every lash reaches him separately, he has fulfilled his oath, and they argued from the generality of this verse. The second opinion is the more probable in this matter, because of the generality of the verse, since what counts is not the specificity of the cause but the generality of the meaning. And Allah knows best. In the story of Job there is an eloquent lesson in training the self and accustoming it to patience, in exercising oneself in facing difficulties and in bearing hardships, and in reviving the ever-radiant hope in the depths of the hearts of the patient.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of oath, governing the genitive; (القرآن) genitive by (الواو), attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أقسم); (ذي) a naʿt (adjective) of القرآن, genitive.
The oath clause: «أقسم بالقرآن ... » has no grammatical position, an initial clause (ibtidāʾiyya).. and the answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "you are indeed one of the messengers" (إنّك لمن المرسلين) [Note: because its parallel is: "Yā Sīn. By the wise Qur'an, you are indeed one of the messengers", and there are many other views of the commentators on the implied answer. What we mentioned is the clearest of them.].

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for iḍrāb (turning from one statement to another); (في عزّة) attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ الذين ...
The clause «الذين كفروا في عزّة ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).

safi-cedvel:3-5.t:
* I'rab:
(كم) khabariyya (declarative, not interrogative), an expression for "many", in the position of an accusative, a fronted direct object; (من قبلهم) attached to (أهلكنا); (من قرن) a tamyīz (specification) of كم; (الفاء) a conjunction; (نادوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, and (الواو) is the fāʿil, referring to the generations, or the nations, or the whole community; (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl; (لات) a negation particle working like ليس, its ism omitted, its implied form being "the time" (الحين); (حين) the one mentioned, the khabar of لات [Note: It is stated in the marginal commentary of al-Jamal: "Abū ʿUbayda said: one pauses at (لا), and the (تاء) is attached to حين, so one says 'I stood tahīna I stood', and 'tahīna such-and-such happened I did such-and-such'.. and he said: I saw it in the imām copy thus: 'lā tahīn', attached. But the codices are in fact لات حين, and the general scholars took what he saw to be among what departs from the script, like its parallels that have passed ..." End of quotation.].
The clause «أهلكنا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نادوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أهلكنا.
The clause «لات حين مناص.» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
(4) (الواو) a conjunction; (أن) a maṣdar particle; (منهم) attached to a naʿt of منذر; (كذّاب) a naʿt of ساحر, nominative [Note: or a second khabar, nominative, of the mubtadaʾ هذا.].
The clause «عجبوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نادوا..
The clause «جاءهم منذر ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن جاءهم ... ) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition attached to (عجبوا), that is: "that there came to them".
The clause «قال الكافرون ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نادوا.
The clause «هذا ساحر ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the speech.
(5) - (الهمزة) for an astonished question (istifhām taʿajjubī); (إلها) a second direct object, accusative; (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis ...
The clause «جعل الآلهة ... » has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the speech «1».
The clause «إنّ هذا لشيء ... » has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the speech «2».

* Morphology:
(3) لات: it is (لا) the negative, and (التاء) is redundant (zāʾida), like its redundancy in ربّ as in their saying ربّت.
(مناص): a maṣdar mīmī from ناصه, that is, "it escaped him", and it is of the pattern قال, or in the sense of "he lagged behind" or "he fled" or "he escaped" ... its wazn is مفعل, and it contains an i'lāl (weakening); its origin is منوص - with fatḥa on the wāw after a quiescent nūn - the fatḥa was moved to the nūn and the wāw made quiescent; then, since what precedes the wāw had fatḥa, the wāw was turned into an alif.
(5) عجاب: an intensive form from the triliteral عجب; its wazn is فعال (with ḍamma on the fāʾ).

* Benefits:
- لات:
The statements of the grammarians conflicted about its reality. The majority hold that it is two words: the negative لا, and the tāʾ marking the feminine of the word, as in ثمة and ربّت. It had to be vowelled because of the meeting of two sukūns.
In support of the majority: one pauses on it with tāʾ and with hāʾ; it was written separate from الحين; and the tāʾ may be given kasra, according to the original vowel for the meeting of two sukūns, whereas if it were a past verb - as some claimed - the kasra would have no basis. As for its operation, some said it governs nothing, and some said that it works like إن. But what the majority of the grammarians hold is that it works like ليس. Its ism comes omitted and only the khabar is mentioned, as in the verse وَلاتَ حِينَ مَناصٍ, the implied form being (ولات الحين حين مناص). There was disagreement about what it governs: al-Farrāʾ stated that it governs only the word الحين, which is the apparent statement of Sībawayh; al-Fārisī and a group held that it governs الحين and what is synonymous with it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: the tāʾ was added to (لا) and it was specialised for negating times.
A benefit:
(ولات حين مناص) was read with a genitive الحين, and al-Farrāʾ claimed that لات is used as a preposition governing the genitive of nouns of time specifically, just as مذ and منذ are, and he cited a verse of Abū Zayd al-Ṭāʾī:
طلبوا صلحنا ولات أوان ... فأجبنا أن لات حين بقاء (They sought our peace, though it was no time ... so we answered that it was no time for staying)
Al-Zamakhsharī rejected this claim, saying:
the origin is (حين مناصهم); then the cutting off of the muḍāf ilayhi from مناص was treated as the cutting off from حين, because of the unity of the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn was made a replacement for the muḍāf ilayhi; then حين was made indeclinable because of its annexation to something not firmly established. Ibn Hishām added: it is better to say that the aforementioned treatment required the indeclinability of حين from the outset, and that مناص is declinable, even if it was truly cut off from annexation, but it is not a time, so it is like "all" and "part".
- Obstinacy and arrogance:
The commentators cited a historical story between the disbelievers of Quraysh and Muḥammad ﷺ as the occasion of revelation of this verse. It is an interesting story, by which you may see the extent of the obstinacy Quraysh had reached, the degree of their insistence on falsehood and their shunning of the truth. The story says:
When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb - may Allah be pleased with him - accepted Islam, this was hard on Quraysh, and the believers rejoiced greatly at it. Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra said to the council of Quraysh, who were the chiefs and nobles, twenty-five men, the oldest of them in age being al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra: "Walk to Abū Ṭālib." They went to him and said to him: "You are our elder and our senior, and you know what these fools have done. We have come to you so that you may judge between us and your nephew." So Abū Ṭālib sent for him and called him, and when he came, the Prophet ﷺ was told: "O son of my brother, these are your people; they ask you for fairness, so do not lean wholly against your people." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And what do they ask of me?" They said: "Abandon us and abandon mention of our gods, and we shall leave you and your God." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you give me one word by which you will rule the Arabs, and by which the non-Arabs will submit to you?" Abū Jahl said: "By your father, we shall give it to you, and ten like it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Say: there is no god but Allah." They recoiled from that and said: "Has he made the gods one God? This is truly an astonishing thing."

safi-cedvel:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (منهم) attached to a ḥāl from الملأ; (أن) a particle of explanation (tafsīr) [Note: or a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive by an omitted (باء), attached to (انطلق).]; (على آلهتكم) attached to (اصبروا), by including in it the meaning "stand firm", that is, stand firm in worshipping them; (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis; and the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (يراد) is a latent pronoun referring to شيء.
The clause «انطلق الملأ ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قال الكافرون [Note: in verse (4) of the sūra.].
The clause «امشوا ... » has no grammatical position, explicative [Note: or it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).].
The clause «اصبروا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause امشوا ...
The clause «إنّ هذا لشيء ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يراد ... » is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of شيء.
(7) - (ما) negative; (بهذا) attached to (سمعنا); (في الملّة) attached to (سمعنا); (إن) a negation particle; (إلّا) for restriction.
The clause «ما سمعنا ... » has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of their objection; and the clause: «إن هذا إلّا اختلاق» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption - or a justification. (8) (الهمزة) for an astonished question; (عليه) attached to (أنزل); (الذكر) the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; (من بيننا) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (عليه); (بل) for transitional iḍrāb in both places; (في شك) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم; (من ذكري) attached to شكّ; (لمّا) a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; (عذاب) a direct object, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, dropped for lightness in keeping with the verse-endings (fawāṣil)... and (الياء) is a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أنزل ... الذكر» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the objection.
The clause «هم في شكّ ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لمّا يذوقوا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive..

* Morphology:
(6) يراد: it contains an i'lāl by substitution suited to the passive; its active form is يريد; when the letter before the last was given fatḥa, and the fatḥa was moved to the letter before the yāʾ after it was made quiescent, the yāʾ was turned into an alif.
(7) اختلاق: a regular maṣdar of the quinqueliteral اختلق; its wazn is افتعال ...

safi-cedvel:45-47.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (إبراهيم) is a badal from عبادنا - or an ʿaṭf bayān on it - accusative; (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places; (أولي) is an adjective of the preceding nouns, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, as it is attached to the sound masculine plural; (الأبصار) is conjoined to الأيدي, genitive.
Clause: «اذكر ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: it may be conjoined to the preceding clause اذكر.].
(46) (إنّا) is a particle resembling the verb, and its ism; (بخالصة) is attached to (أخلصناهم); (ذكرى) is a badal from خالصة, genitive like it [Note: if (خالصة) is a maṣdar, it is permissible for (ذكرى) to be a direct object whose operator is the maṣdar..
And it is permissible for (ذكرى) to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي", and the clause is an adjective of خالصة.]; and the clause «إنّا أخلصناهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «أخلصناهم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(47) (الواو) is a conjunction; (عندنا) is an accusative adverb attached to المصطفين; (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis; (من المصطفين) is attached to the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «إنّهم ... لمن المصطفين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّا أخلصناهم.

* Morphology:
(المصطفين): plural of المصطفى, a passive participle from the five-letter verb اصطفى; its wazn is مفتعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn, and it contains an iʿlāl by omission: the alif was omitted because it met the quiescent yāʾ (of the plural) as a quiescent letter, and the fatḥa was left on the fāʾ as an indication of the omitted alif, so its wazn is المفتعين.. And it contains the substitution of the tāʾ of the ifti'āl form by ṭāʾ because it comes after the ṣād; its origin is المصتفين.
(الأخيار): plural of خيّر, a sifa mushabbaha from خار يخير of the bāb ضرب; its wazn is فيعل, and the yāʾ of فيعل has been assimilated into the ʿayn of the word; the wazn of أخيار is أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
Al-majāz al-mursal (loose metonymy): in His saying, the Exalted: «أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصارِ».
الأيد is a majāz mursal for strength, and الأبصار is the plural of بصر meaning insight (baṣīra), which is also a majāz.
Or: "possessors of glorious deeds and noble knowledge", on the basis that mentioning the hands is mentioning the cause while intending the effect, and الأبصار, meaning insights, is a majāz for the knowledge that branches out from them.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive and the second is a conjunction; (ذا) is conjoined to إسماعيل, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the alif; (من الأخيار) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ كلّ.
Clause: «اذكر ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the preceding clause اذكر, either mentioned or implied.].
And the clause «كلّ من الأخيار ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(اليسع): a prophet of the Children of Israel, the son of Akhṭūb..
Elijah (Ilyās) appointed him as successor over the Children of Israel, and then he was made a prophet. His word is foreign (aʿjamī); and it is said that it is derived from الوسع.

safi-cedvel:49-54.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (للمتّقين) is attached to the khabar of إنّ; (اللام) is for emphasis; (حسن) is the ism of إنّ, postponed, accusative.
Clause: «هذا ذكر..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّ للمتّقين لحسن ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(50-51) (جنّات) is an ʿaṭf bayān on حسن; (مفتّحة) is a ḥāl from جنّات عدن, and the operator in it is the meaning of a verb contained in المتّقين, and the linking pronoun is implied, i.e. "from them"; (لهم) is attached to مفتّحة; (الأبواب) is the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive participle مفتّحة; (متّكئين) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in (لهم); (فيها) is attached to متّكئين, and the second is attached to (يدعون); (بفاكهة) is attached to (يدعون).
And the clause «يدعون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in متّكئين [Note: or a second ḥāl from the pronoun in (لهم).. or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumptive.].
(52) (الواو) is a conjunction; (عندهم) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ قاصرات; (أتراب) is a badal from قاصرات - or an adjective of it - nominative.
And the clause «عندهم قاصرات..» is conjoined to the clause يدعون and takes its position in i'rab.
(53) (ما) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هذا, and the (الواو) in (توعدون) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (ليوم) is attached to (توعدون).
And the clause «هذا ما توعدون ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying of an implied saying ...
And the clause «توعدون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
(54) (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis; (ما) is a negative particle that is inoperative (muhmala); (له) is attached to a fronted khabar; (نفاد) is genitive in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
And the clause «إنّ هذا لرزقنا..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «ما له من نفاد..» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from رزقنا.

* Morphology:
(50) مفتّحة: the feminine of مفتّح, a passive participle from the quadriliteral (فتح) [Translator's note: the source says quadriliteral; the verb is the form فعّل]; its wazn is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(52) أتراب: plural of ترب, a sifa mushabbaha from the quadriliteral تأرب, meaning "to be equal in age", and it is used for both masculine and feminine; its wazn is فعل with kasra then sukūn, and the wazn of أتراب is أفعال.
(54) نفاد: a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb نفد of the bāb فرح; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and there is another maṣdar, نفذ, with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:71-74.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) is an adverb of past time, a badal from the first adverb [Note: in verse (69) of this sūra.. It is also permissible for it to be an adverbial noun in the position of accusative, a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر.]; (للملائكة) is attached to (قال); (بشرا) is a direct object of the active participle خالق; (من طين) is attached to an adjective of (بشرا).
Clause: «قال ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «إنّي خالق ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
(72) (الفاء) is a conjunction, and likewise the (الواو); (فيه) is attached to (نفخت); (من روحي) is attached to (نفخت); (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis; (له) is attached to (قعوا), by implying in it the meaning of "prostrate" [Note: or attached to ساجدين.]; (ساجدين) is a ḥāl, accusative, from the agent of قعوا.
And the clause «سوّيته ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «نفخت ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause سوّيته.
And the clause «قعوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(73) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (كلّهم) is a tawkīd maʿnawī (semantic emphasis) for الملائكة, nominative; (أجمعون) is a second semantic emphasis, nominative.
And the clause «سجد الملائكة ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: "So He created him, fashioned him, breathed the spirit into him, and the angels prostrated."
(74) (إلّا) is for exception; (إبليس) is accusative as an exception, either discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ) or continuous (muttaṣil) according to the interpretation of the meaning of إبليس; (من الكافرين) is attached to the khabar of كان.
And the clause «استكبر ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «كان من الكافرين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause استكبر.

* Morphology:
(72) قعوا: it contains an iʿlāl by omission, being a weak verb of the type mithāl (with weak first radical) whose fāʾ is omitted in the imperfect and the imperative; its wazn is علوا with fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) أم, meaning بل and the hamza; (عندهم) an accusative adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ خزائن; (العزيز) a naʿt of (ربّك), genitive; (الوهّاب) a second naʿt, genitive.
The clause «عندهم خزائن..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(10) (أم) like the first; (لهم) attached to a khabar of the mubtadaʾ ملك; (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (ما) a relative noun in the position of a genitive, conjoined to السموات; (بينهما) an accusative adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; (الفاء) a connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition; (اللام) the lām of command; (في الأسباب) attached to (يرتقوا).
The clause «لهم ملك ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ليرتقوا ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if they claim what they say, then let them ascend."
(11) (جند) a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "they" (هم) [Note: or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is مهزوم, and (هنالك) a naʿt of جند.]; (ما) redundant, for belittlement [Note: (ما) may be a naʿt of جند by way of belittlement or magnification, to mock them.]; (هنالك) a demonstrative in the position of an accusative, an adverb of place attached to a naʿt of جند [Note: it may be attached to an omitted khabar of جند, or attached to (مهزوم).]; (مهزوم) a naʿt of جند, nominative; (من الأحزاب) attached to a naʿt of جند.
The clause « (هم) جند ... » has no grammatical position, giving a reason (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(مهزوم): a passive participle from the triliteral هزم; its wazn is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:12-15.t:
* I'rab:
(قبلهم) an accusative adverb attached to (كذّبت); (الواو) a conjunction in all five places.
The clause «كذّبت قبلهم قوم..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أولئك الأحزاب..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
(14) - (إن) a negation particle; (كلّ) a mubtadaʾ, nominative, dependent on a negation [Note: or on what denotes generality.]; (إلّا) for restriction; (الفاء) a conjunction; (عقاب) a fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, in keeping with the verse-ending, and (الياء) is a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إن كلّ إلّا كذّب ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption [Note: it may be a khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك if (الأحزاب) is parsed as a badal from the demonstrative.].
The clause «حقّ عقاب..» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause كذّب..
(15) (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) negative; (إلّا) for restriction; (صيحة) a direct object, accusative; (ما) like the first; (لها) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ فواق; (فواق) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «ما ينظر هؤلاء إلّا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن كلّ إلّا [Note: it may be resumptive.].
The clause «ما لها من فواق..» is in the position of an accusative, a second naʿt of صيحة [Note: or a ḥāl from صيحة because it is a descriptive.].

* Morphology:
(12) الأوتاد: plural of وتد, a name for what is driven into the ground or a wall; its wazn is فعل (with fatḥa then kasra).
(15) فواق: it is said to be a noun of a verbal noun (ism maṣdar) from أفاق, like الجواب from أجاب; its wazn is فعال (with fatḥa on the fāʾ).. and it is said to be a noun meaning the span of time that lies between two milkings; it is reported in the hadith: "Visiting the sick is the length of a fawāq of a she-camel"; and it is said to mean "return", its plural أفواق ... and the plural of the plural أفاويق....

* Rhetoric:
The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو الْأَوْتادِ».
Here Pharaoh, in the garments of his kingship and the firmness of his sovereignty, is likened to a firm house whose pillar has been raised and whose pegs have been fixed - a simile kept hidden in the soul, in the manner of the implicit metaphor. He is described as "possessor of the pegs" by way of imaginative attribution (takhyīl). It is also said: the firm kingdom, in respect of its firmness and steadiness, is likened to "the possessor of the pegs", that is, the tent stretched with its pegs, and "the possessor of the pegs" is borrowed for it by way of the explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya).

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ربّنا) the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative; (لنا) attached to (عجّل); (قبل) an accusative adverb of time attached to (عجّل)..
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The vocative clause and its response ... is in the position of an accusative, the content of the speech.
The clause «عجّل ... » has no grammatical position, the response to the vocative.

* Morphology:
(قطّنا ... ): a noun meaning "share" and "portion", from the triliteral قطّ meaning "to cut"; it is also applied to a scroll, a written document, and a prize; its wazn is فعل (with kasra then sukūn), its plural قطوط (with ḍamma on the qāf) and قططة (with kasra then fatḥa), and the plural of paucity أقططة and أقطاط ...

safi-cedvel:17-23.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, that is, "what they say of it"], (داود) an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to عبدنا, accusative; (ذا) a naʿt of داود, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the alif.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يقولون ... ) is in the position of a genitive, attached to (اصبر).
The clause «اصبر ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
The clause «اذكر ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصبر.
The clause «إنّه أوّاب..» has no grammatical position, a justification for His saying (ذا الأيد).
(18) (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, with its ism; (معه) an accusative adverb attached to (يسبّحن); (بالعشي) attached to (يسبّحن).
The clause «إنّا سخرنا ... » has no grammatical position, a resumption in the course of the story of Dāwūd.
The clause «سخرّنا..» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
The clause «يسبّحن..» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from الجبال.
(19) (الطير) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "we subjected" (سخرّنا); (محشورة) a ḥāl, accusative, from الطير; (كلّ) a mubtadaʾ, nominative; (له) attached to أوّاب.
The clause « (سخرّنا) الطير..» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause سخرنا الجبال.
The clause «كلّ له أوّاب ... » has no grammatical position, a resumption confirming the content of what precedes it.
(20) (الواو) a conjunction in the three places; (الحكمة) a second direct object, accusative.
The clause «شددنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause سخّرنا الجبال.
The clause «آتيناه ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause سخّرنا الجبال.
(21-23) (الواو) a conjunction; (هل) an interrogative particle for arousing interest; (إذ) an adverb of past time attached to نبإ [Note: this is the choice of Abū al-Baqāʾ, and al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask, with what is (إذ) put in the accusative? I say: it cannot be other than that it is put in the accusative by (أتاك), or by النبأ, or by an omitted word. Its being put in the accusative by (أتاك) is not allowable, because the coming of the report occurs only in his time (the Prophet's), not in the time of Dāwūd; and its attachment to (النبأ) is not allowable because the event occurred in the time of Dāwūd, so its coming to the Messenger of Allah would not be sound.. So what remains is that it is put in the accusative by an omitted word, its implied form being: the report of the litigation of the two adversaries.. but this restriction involves strain, for the report that occurred in the time of Dāwūd comes to the Messenger of Allah by way of transmission."]; (إذ) the second, in the position of an accusative, a badal from the first [Note: it may be attached to (تسوّروا)]; (على داود) attached to (دخلوا); (الفاء) a conjunction; (منهم) attached to (فزع); (لا) prohibitive, jussive; (خصمان) a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "we" (نحن); (على بعض) attached to (بغى); (الفاء) a connecting particle for the apodosis of an implied condition; (بيننا) an accusative adverb attached to (احكم); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of احكم; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) like the first; (الواو) a conjunction; (إلى سواء) attached to (اهدنا); (أخي) the khabar of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is a muḍāf ilayhi [Note: (أخي) may be a badal from the demonstrative, and the khabar is the clause له تسع..]; (له) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ تسع; (نعجة) a tamyīz, accusative; (لي) like له, and the mubtadaʾ is نعجة; and (النون) in (أكفلنيها) is the nūn of protection, and (الياء) is the first direct object and (ها) the second direct object; (في الخطاب) attached to (عزّني).
The clause «هل أتاك..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اصبر.
The clause «تسوّروا ... » is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «دخلوا ... » is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «فزع ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause دخلوا.
The clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لا تخف ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the speech.
The clause « (نحن) خصمان ... » has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the speech [Note: or it is a justification for the prohibition of fear.].
The clause «بغى بعضنا..» is in the position of a nominative, a naʿt of (خصمان).
The clause «احكم ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you hear our story, then judge."
The clause «لا تشطط..» is conjoined to the clause احكم..
The clause «اهدنا ... » is conjoined to the clause احكم.
The clause «إنّ هذا أخي ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption [Note: or it is the content of an implied saying, that is, "one of them said: this is my brother ..."].
The clause «له تسع ... » is in the position of a nominative, a second khabar of (إنّ).
The clause «لي نعجة..» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause له تسع.
The clause «قال ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لي نعجة.
The clause «أكفلنيها..» is in the position of an accusative, the content of the speech.
The clause «عزّني ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause قال.

* Morphology:
(محشورة): a passive participle from the triliteral حشر; its masculine is محشور, wazn مفعول.
(الخطاب): a noun denoting speech; in origin it is an audited (samāʿī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral خاطب; its wazn is فعال (with kasra on the fāʾ).
(23) نعجة: an inert noun for the female sheep, and it has been used figuratively for a woman; its wazn is فعلة (with fatḥa then sukūn).

* Rhetoric:
1- Shifting from the nominal to the verbal form: in His saying, the Exalted, «يُسَبِّحْنَ».
The shift from "glorifying ones" (مسبحات), although the basic rule for the ḥāl is the singular form (a non-clausal word), is to indicate the renewal of glorification, state after state, like the verse of al-Aʿshā:
لعمري لقد لاحت عيون كثيرة ... إلى ضوء نار في يفاع تحرق (By my life, many eyes have looked toward the light of a fire burning on a height)
Had he said "burning" (محرقة, nominal participle) it would not have had that impact.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq): in His saying, the Exalted, «بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِشْراقِ» there is a beautiful antithesis between the evening prayer and the forenoon prayer.

* Benefits:
1- (ذا الأيد): ذا means "possessor of", and it is one of the five nouns (al-asmāʾ al-khamsa) in the accusative case. The five nouns are nominative with wāw, such as: أخوك طالب نظيف - ذو العقل يشقى في النعيم بعقله.
b- And the five nouns are accusative with alif, such as: إن أخاك تلميذ نشيط.
c- And the five nouns are genitive with yāʾ, such as: كم لأخيك من فضل عليك, كن عونا لذي الحاجة.
The five nouns are not declined in this manner except under the following conditions:
a- That they be singular (neither dual nor plural).
b- That they be in the full form (not diminutive). c- That they be annexed to something other than the yāʾ of the first person.
2- (كلّ), tanwīn of compensation (tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ): it is either a compensation for a singular, which is what attaches to كلا, بعضا and أيّا as compensation for what they are annexed to, such as: كلّ له أواب, that is, "everything is turning to Him", or a compensation for a clause, which is what attaches to إذ as compensation for a clause following it, such as: «فَلَوْلا إِذا بَلَغَتِ الْحُلْقُومَ وَأَنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ», that is:
"when the soul reaches the throat".
In writing: tanwīn is two fatḥas placed at the end of an indefinite noun that is free of the definite article (ال) and of annexation, such as: رجلا, رجل, رجل [Translator's note: the source shows these three forms, apparently meant to show the three tanwīn markings (fatḥatān, ḍammatān, kasratān); they are reproduced as written.].
3- (تسع وتسعون) numbers are of two kinds:
a- Explicit (ṣarīḥ): the defined numbers b- Vague (mubham): that which is indicated by the numeral substitutes (كم - كأين - كذا). A number, explicit or vague, needs a tamyīz to remove its vagueness. The rules for the tamyīz of numbers we summarise as follows:
a- Numbers from (3-10): their tamyīz is a plural, genitive by annexation, such as (قرأت ثلاثة كتب).
b- Numbers from (11-99): their tamyīz is a singular, accusative, such as: (إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً).
c- Numbers (100) and (1000) and their multiples: their tamyīz is a singular, genitive by annexation, such as (مائة رجل، وألف طفل، ومائتا امرأة).

safi-cedvel:75-75.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; (لما) is attached to (تسجد), and the returning pronoun is omitted; (بيديّ) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of خلقت; (the hamza) is for reproachful interrogation; (أم) is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction; (من العالين) is the khabar of كنت.
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the vocative clause and its response are in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying [Note: it is permissible for the vocative clause to be parenthetical and the clause ما منعك to be the content of the saying.].
And the clause «ما منعك أن تسجد ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause «تسجد ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied literal particle (أن).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تسجد) is in the position of genitive by an omitted (من), attached to (منعك), i.e. "what prevented you from prostrating".
And the clause «خلقت ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «استكبرت» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive within the scope of the saying.
And the clause «كنت من العالين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause استكبرت.

* Rhetoric:
Taghlīb (giving precedence): in His saying, the Exalted: «ما مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ».
It gives precedence to the two hands over the other limbs with which deeds are carried out, because one who has two hands performs most of his deeds with his hands, so working with the hands prevailed over all other deeds performed by other means, until it was said of an action of the heart: it is among what your hands have done, and until it was said to one who has no hand: "Your hands tied the skin and your mouth blew into it," and until no difference remained between your saying: "this is among what I have done" and "this is among what your hands have done." Of this is His saying, the Exalted, «مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينا» and «لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ».

safi-cedvel:76-76.t:
* I'rab:
(منه) is attached to خير, and the nūn in (خلقتني) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya); (من نار) is attached to (خلقتني); (من طين) to (خلقته).
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «أنا خير منه ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «خلقتني ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive - or gives a reason - and the clause «خلقته ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خلقتني.

safi-cedvel:77-78.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis; (منها) is attached to (اخرج); (الفاء) gives a reason.
Clause: «قال..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اخرج منها ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if you refuse to prostrate, then go out.." and the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «إنّك رجيم ...» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
(78) (الواو) is a conjunction; (عليك) is attached to an omitted khabar of إنّ; (إلى يوم) is attached to (لعنتي).
And the clause «إنّ عليك لعنتي ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنك رجيم.

safi-cedvel:79-79.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) is a vocative muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ that is omitted for lightness.. and the (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis; (إلى يوم) is attached to (أنظرني), and the second (النون) in the verb is for protection, and the wāw in (يبعثون) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the vocative clause and its response ... are in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying [Note: it is permissible for the vocative clause to be parenthetical, and the condition and its apodosis to be the content of the saying.] And the clause «أنظرني ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if You have made me accursed, then grant me respite ..."
And the clause «يبعثون» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.

safi-cedvel:80-81.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis; (من المنظرين) is attached to the khabar of إنّ; (إلى يوم) is attached to المنظرين.
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «إنّك من المنظرين» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.:
"if you desire respite, then you are among those granted respite.." and the condition, its verb and its apodosis are in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.

safi-cedvel:82-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is for the connection of the clause's sequence to the granting of respite; (الباء) is the bāʾ of the oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear); (اللام) is the lām of the oath; (أجمعين) is an emphasis for the object pronoun in (أغوينّهم) [Note: or an accusative ḥāl, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.].
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «(أقسم) بعزّتك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "أنا", and the nominal clause is the apodosis of the implied condition, i.e.: "if You grant me respite, then I swear ... I will surely mislead them", and the condition and the apodosis are the content of the saying.
And the clause «أغوينّهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the oath.
(82) (إلّا) is for exception; (عبادك) is accusative as a discontinuous - or continuous - exception; (منهم) is attached to المخلصين [Note: many of the grammarians refuse this attachment because the operand of the ṣila precedes the relative noun, but the Qur'anic style does not prevent that.].

safi-cedvel:84-85.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis; the first (الحقّ) is a mubtadaʾ, nominative, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "منّي" (from Me) [Note: or "my oath", or the clause of the oath and its response ... It is also permissible for الحقّ to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "أنا" or "قولي".]; (الواو) is parenthetical; the second (الحقّ) is a fronted direct object, accusative.
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «الحقّ (منّي)» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if they go astray through you, then the truth is from Me ..." and the condition and its apodosis are the content of the saying.
And the clause «أقول ...» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
(85) (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (منك) is attached to (أملأن), and likewise (ممن); (منهم) is attached to a ḥāl from the returning pronoun; (أجمعين) is a semantic emphasis for the pronoun in (منك) and what is conjoined to it [Note: al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be an emphasis for the pronoun in (منهم).], genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
And the clause «أملأن ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause is in the position of accusative, a badal from الحقّ, the object of أقول [Note: or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumptive.].
And the clause «تبعك ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

safi-cedvel:86-88.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) is negative; (عليه) is attached to أجر; (أجر) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a second direct object; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negative, working as ليس [Note: or inoperative, and the pronoun (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ], (من المتكلّفين) is attached to the khabar of ما [Note: or attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنا.]. Clause: «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «ما أسألكم ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «ما أنا من المتكلّفين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of the saying.
(87) (إن) is negative; (إلّا) is for restriction; (للعالمين) is attached to ذكر - or to an adjective of ذكر -.
And the clause «إن هو إلّا ذكر ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive within the scope of the saying.
(88) The wāw is a conjunction; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (تعلمنّ) is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of similar letters, and the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; and the (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (بعد) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (تعلمنّ) [Note: or attached to the second object of (تعلمن) if "knowing" is in its usual sense, so that it takes two objects.].
And the clause «تعلمنّ ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the implied oath, and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إن هو إلّا ذكر.

* Morphology:
(المتكلّفين): plural of المتكلّف, an active participle from the five-letter verb تكلّف; its wazn is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn..

safi-cedvel:24-26.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of certainty; (بسؤال) attached to (ظلمك); (إلى نعاجه) attached to an omitted word that is annexed to نعجتك, that is, "the request to add your ewe"; (الواو) a conjunction; (من الخلطاء) attached to a naʿt of (كثيرا); (اللام) the shifted lām for emphasis; (على بعض) attached to (يبغي); (إلّا) for exception; (الذين) a relative in the position of an accusative by connected exception; (الواو) a conjunction and the second one parenthetical; (قليل) a fronted khabar, nominative; (ما) redundant, to emphasise fewness; (هم) a detached pronoun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; (الواو) a conjunction; (أنّما) restraining and restrained (kāffa and makfūfa); (الفاء) a conjunction; (راكعا) a ḥāl, accusative, from the fāʿil of خرّ.
The clause «قال ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ظلمك» has no grammatical position, the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause with its answer is in the position of an accusative, the content of the speech.
The clause «إنّ كثيرا.. ليبغي بعضهم» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the content of the speech [Note: or conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath, in which case it has no position.].
The clause «يبغي بعضهم..» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of inna.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنوا..
The clause «قليل ما هم ... » has no grammatical position, parenthetical..
The clause «ظنّ داود..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قال ...
The clause «أنّما فتّناه ... » is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّ [Note: it is in reality not a clause but an interpreted maṣdar, because the restraining (ما) does not take (أنّ) out of being a maṣdar particle but only restrains it from operating.].
The clause «استغفر ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ظنّ.
The clause «أناب ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استغفر.
The clause «خرّ ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استغفر.
(25) (الفاء) a conjunction; (له) attached to (غفرنا), and the reference in (ذلك) is to the sin; (الواو) a conjunction; (له) the second, attached to the khabar of inna; (عندنا) an accusative adverb attached to the khabar [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from زلفى.]; (اللام) for emphasis; (زلفي) the ism of inna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa.
The clause «غفرنا له ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استغفر ...
The clause «إنّ له ... لزلفى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause غفرنا [Note: the clause may be circumstantial.. or resumptive, to confirm the content of what precedes.].
(26) (خليفة) a second direct object, accusative; (في الأرض) attached to a naʿt of خليفة; (الفاء) to link the effect to the cause; (بين) an accusative adverb attached to (احكم); (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil of احكم; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, jussive, and the verb (تتّبع) was vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns; (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation; (يضلّك) an imperfect verb put in the accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ; (عن سبيل) attached to (يضلّ).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضلّك..) is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the preceding prohibition, that is: "let there be no following of desire on your part, which would lead to its misleading you from the path of Allah."
(عن سبيل) the second, attached to (يضلّون), that is, "they stray far"; (لهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ عذاب; (ما) a maṣdar particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما نسوا..) is in the position of a genitive by (الباء), attached to (عذاب ... ), and (الباء) denotes cause (sababiyya).
(يوم) is a direct object whose operator is نسوا [Note: it may be an adverb attached to عذاب, with the object of نسوا implied..].
